summary: For its first thirty years this district was a set of avenue names being graded into existence — Plymouth, Capitol, Orizaba, Miramar, Faxon, Harold, Lee, Jules — with contractors given ninety days at a time, and some of them losing the work when they ran over. An arc lamp went up at Orizaba and Sagamore in 1908. In 1909 the president of the Ocean View Improvement Club was licensed to blast rock out of the ground at Thrift Street and Lakeview Avenue. In 1916 the Board asked that a pool of water at Farallones Street and San Jose Avenue be filled in, two boys having drowned in it. In 1921 it asked for a playground beside the Sheridan School and for a park opposite the railway station. At the end of the twenties Alemany Boulevard was cut through in lettered sections, and a house at 102 Bright Street was sold off out of its way. Then the record thins for decades and comes back along Ocean Avenue: a twenty-nine-lot subdivision at 1 Capitol Avenue in 2013, a landmark in 2016 for the Ingleside Presbyterian Church and its Great Cloud of Witnesses at 1345 Ocean Avenue, and then — three times in six months of 2024 — an ordinance requiring that the new branch library for Oceanview, Merced Heights, Ingleside and Lakeview be built on the city's own ground at 100 Orizaba Avenue.
